title: An optogenetic tool to inhibit RhoA in Drosophila embryos
protocol: Place an orange-red plastic shield on the stage of an upright Nikon SMZ-745 stereoscope in preparation for embryo collection.
Change the apple juice plate at the time of embryo collection.
Cover the surface of the plate taken off from the cup with a thin layer of Halocarbon oil 27.
Collect 5–15 embryos at the desired stage using Dumont Style 5 tweezers.
Remove excess oil from embryos by gently blotting them on a small piece of paper towel.
Dechorionate embryos using fresh 40% bleach (∼3% sodium hypochlorite) for about 2 minutes.
Pick up the paper towel with tweezers and place it on a large tissue paper to absorb excessive bleach.
Rinse embryos using deionized water, repeating the process of soaking and drying the paper towel in deionized water for 8 times.
Transfer the dechorionated embryo from the square paper towel to a 35-mm glass-bottom dish using an eyelash tool.
Add deionized water to the well in the middle of the dish to completely cover the well.
Use the eyelash tool to gently adjust the embryos to the desired position and orientation for imaging.
Transfer the 35-mm glass-bottom dish with the embryos to the confocal or multiphoton microscope.
Protect embryos from ambient light or other light sources associated with the microscope.
Set up the sample for the Olympus FVMPE-RS multiphoton system.
Use a black cloth cover to protect samples during optogenetic experiments.
Transfer the sample to the microscope stage.
Turn off all light sources, including room and computer monitors.
Use the eyepiece to identify the embryo of interest.
Bring the embryo into focus using non-blue light illumination.
Illuminate the specimen with green excitation light (532–554 nm) using the TRITC filter set.
Cover the microscope with a black cloth to protect the sample from unwanted light.
Set up the sample for the inverted Nikon spinning disk confocal microscope.
Transfer the sample to the microscope stage with all light sources turned off.
Place an orange-red plastic shield on top of the sample.
Turn on the transmitted light for sample illumination.
Use the transmitted light for adjusting the position of the stage and focus of the embryo.
Ensure there is no ambient light in the room before taking the sample out of the light-proof transfer box.
Turn off or cover all controllers and open light sources when the sample is not protected from ambient light.
Keep the orange-red plastic shield on top of the sample throughout the entire stimulation and imaging process to avoid accidental stimulation by ambient light.
Use the Olympus FVMPE-RS multiphoton microscope for pre-stimulation, stimulation, and post-stimulation imaging.
Employ different lasers in the multiphoton microscope system to achieve pre-stimulation imaging, stimulation, and post-stimulation imaging.
Turn off or cover all light sources in the room before taking the sample out of the transfer box.
Place the 35 mm glass-bottom dish on the stage and locate the embryos using the eyepiece.
Filter out the blue light component using a filter to avoid unwanted stimulation.
Cover the microscope with a light-proof black cloth.
Ensure the sample is fully protected from light before turning on the computer screen and other necessary light sources.
Acquire pre-stimulation movies using the 1,040 nm laser.
Use laser intensity ranging from 4% to 10%, with a linear increase in laser intensity from embryo surface to a depth of 100 μm for optimal imaging.
Scan a defined region of interest with a blue laser (400 nm–500 nm).
Stimulate the sample using a 488-nm blue laser when imaging GFP- or YFP-tagged proteins on a spinning disk confocal microscope.
Stimulate the sample by scanning a defined region of interest with a 920-nm laser on a multiphoton microscope.
Use a separate photo-stimulation/photo-activation module equipped on the microscope for stimulation, as described above.
Acquire post-stimulation movies using both 1,040 nm and 920 nm lasers.
Imaging Sqh-GFP using a single photon laser.
Adjust blue laser intensity for exciting GFP.
Ensure blue laser intensity is lower than that required for stimulating the optogenetic module.
Avoid scattering of blue laser from embryos during post-stimulation imaging.
Adjust laser intensity based on expression levels of fluorescent markers.
Achieve optimal signal-to-noise ratio while avoiding photobleaching of fluorophores.
Note activation of the optogenetic module by blue light is reversible.
Observe slower dissociation rate after turning off stimulation compared to light-induced dimerization.
Monitor membrane recruitment of CRY2-Rho1DN-mCherry visible up to 10-15 minutes post-stimulation.
Turn off or cover room lights and computer screens before taking the sample out of the transfer box.
Ensure no ambient light is present in the room.
Place the 35-mm glass-bottom dish on the microscope stage.
Place an orange-red plastic shield above the dish to protect it from unwanted stimulation.
Block any light from the computer screen that might stimulate the sample.
Turn on the transmitted light through software control and locate the embryo with the eyepiece.
Acquire a pre-stimulation movie using the 561 nm laser.
Set laser intensity to 20% for imaging Sqh-mCherry in early embryos.
Adjust laser intensity empirically for pre- and post-stimulation imaging to achieve optimal signal-to-noise ratio while minimizing photobleaching.
Use the 488 nm laser at an intensity of 10%-20% for simultaneous stimulation of optogenetic module and acquisition of GFP signal.
Acquire signals in the mCherry channel using the 561 nm laser simultaneously with GFP imaging.
